text: **AFTER `organize`, THE TREE HOLDS ONLY WHAT `.intentfiles` NAMES -- ASSERTED AS AN EQUALITY OF TWO INDEPENDENTLY DERIVED SETS, OVER THE WHOLE ESTATE.** (hv 2026-08-18, stating the expectation explicitly for the record.) The on-disk population is derived by LISTING THE FILESYSTEM and the declared population by PARSING `.intentfiles`; the criterion is `on_disk == declared`, **printed with both counts, and it is an EQUALITY rather than a containment in either direction** -- a subset check passes on a tree that removed nothing, and a superset check passes on an empty one. **THE REASON THIS ROW EXISTS: EVERY ONE OF ST0057 AC-04.1 THROUGH AC-04.5 IS SATISFIED BY AN `organize` THAT REMOVES NOTHING AT ALL.** Report-never-remove (04.1), refuse-on-hand-edit (04.2), never-resolve-a-divergence (04.3), run-twice-changes-nothing (04.4), refuse-on-digest-change (04.5). **They are all BRAKES, correctly specified, and not one of them says the car moves.** D57-3's table declares DEHYDRATE as an action and AC-04.1 requires every row EXERCISED, **which one dehydrated file satisfies** -- a subset of the right kind, which is the EXTENT failure this estate has now met three times. **THE POSITIVE CONTROL IS PART OF THE CRITERION, NOT THE TEST'S BUSINESS:** it must be driven FROM A FULLY REALISED TREE, because a run against an already-sparse fixture is the vacuous pass. **Measured at `ddf8a080`, before any of this lands: `intent/st/` holds 57 ST directories and 799 files, `intent/issues/` holds 40 canon files and 82 files total.** Those are the numbers the first real run must move. **INDEX VIEWS ARE NAMED, NOT INFERRED.** `intent/st/steel_threads.md` is renderer-produced but is not a per-artefact view and does not appear in the manifest; it and anything like it are declared as an explicit exempt set with the reason, **rather than left to be caught by D57-3's fifth row** -- UNCLAIMED means _a human put this here_, and using it to shelter something the renderer DOES produce would make the report meaningless. Attachments remain out by AC-04.3.
